newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Last land mines in Guatemala will be destroyed-U.N..
newsitem.headline: Last land mines in Guatemala will be destroyed-U.N..

text.p: Guatemala's former guerrillas have pledged to destroy within one month the last 350 land mines still buried in the western highlands, a United Nations monitor said on Wednesday.

The leftist former guerrillas of the Guatemalan National Revolutionary Unit (URNG) have been living in eight disarmament camps across the country in recent weeks following the historic Dec. 29 peace accord signed with the government.

The only remaining minefield identified by the URNG lies on the slopes of the Tajumulco Volcano, the country's highest, about 25 miles (40 km) from the western border with Mexico, said Gen. Jose B. Rodriguez of Spain, head of the 155-member unarmed U.N. military force monitoring the peace process.

Those mines will be eliminated "by the URNG itself, with the support of the government, the army and of course the United Nations, a process that should begin today since the camps are established," Rodriguez told a news conference.

Rebel leaders provided a map of the mines. The army will do technical work and the U.N. will mark the area before the explosives are detonated. The process should take less than a month, Rodriguez said.

Rebel disarmament is one aspect of 11 complex and comprehensive accords that put an end to 36 years of civil war. The agreement calls for the rebels to hand over all arms and reveal the location of buried weapons and explosives.
